key_insight: PathAgentBench shows that vision-language models can reason over curated pathology evidence well, but still struggle to find that evidence directly in whole-slide images.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark highlights a major gap for digital pathology AI: accurate diagnosis depends not just on interpretation, but on locating diagnostically relevant regions across magnifications.
method: Built a diagnostic-tree benchmark linking nested WSI regions across scales with evidence and diagnosis labels
Evaluated four capabilities: image-text matching, text-image retrieval, region localization, and multi-scale reasoning
Tested 20 general-purpose, medical, and pathology-specialized models plus an autonomous exploration setting
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 1,822 TCGA whole-slide images, 17,135 diagnostic paths, and a private set of 190 breast cancer WSIs annotated by ten board-certified pathologists.
watch_item: Region localization remains very weak, so high reasoning scores may overstate real-world slide-level performance when models cannot reliably acquire the needed evidence.
paper_title: PathAgentBench: Benchmarking Evidence-Seeking Vision-Language Models on Whole-Slide Pathology Image
